What are the common methods used to discharge an insulator? Briefly elaborate any one method.
modelAnswer: An insulator can be discharged by heating it above a flame or by exposing it to humid conditions. Heating excites electrons and makes the surrounding air conductive; humidity lets a thin conductive water layer carry charge away.

stem: Describe the construction of an electroscope. Make its diagram. How can we detect: a. Presence of charge and b. Nature of charge on the body.
modelAnswer: An electroscope detects charge because like charges repel. A metal disk and rod conduct charge to two thin leaves, which separate when similarly charged. Comparing the leaf response with a body of known sign allows the presence and nature of charge to be determined.

stem: Define electric field. How is it expressed mathematically? Is it a vector quantity?
modelAnswer: An electric field is the region around a charge where it exerts a force on other charges. Its strength is E = F/q₀, where F is the force on a positive test charge q₀. Electric-field intensity is a vector quantity, so it has both magnitude and direction.
keyPoints: ["Define electric field as the region around a charge where it exerts force.","Use E = F/q₀ for field strength.","State that electric field intensity is a vector with magnitude and direction."]
